Adjusted tone using SLOOS: The July 2021 Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey indicates a broad-based improvement in credit conditions—banks reported stronger demand for C&I loans across large, middle-market, and small firms, higher borrower inquiries, and easing in terms; consumer loan standards (credit card, auto, other) also eased. Foreign bank branches likewise reported stronger C&I demand tied to inventory, accounts receivable, capex, and M&A. These are pro-cyclical signals that reinforce the statement’s claim that financial conditions are accommodative and that the flow of credit is supporting households and businesses. While some terms remained tighter relative to 2019 in select areas and foreign banks reported largely unchanged C&I terms, the net SLOOS picture is positive and warrants a modestly higher sentiment than previously assigned. Balancing this with the statement’s cautions—elevated (largely transitory) inflation, pandemic risks, and a signal that tapering may soon be warranted—yields a moderately positive but still tempered assessment.
